messages.subject: New versions of RSQLite and DBI break sqldf
messages.subject_clean: New versions of RSQLite and DBI break sqldf
messages.body_plain:
New versions of DBI and RSQLite have been released which break sqldf.

Until sqldf is updated please revert to the DBI 0.3.1 and RSQLite 0.11.4.

An easy way to revert is to use the checkpoint package as shown here:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/26571232/sqldf-not-working-after-update

messages.subject: Bug in where
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have used the below query from the Auto data set in the ISLR library.

sqldf("select a.mpg,count(distinct a.name <http://a.name>) from Auto2 a  join Auto b on a.cylinders = b.cylinders where a.cylinders=6  and b.name <http://b.name>=='buick century limited' group by a.mpg order by 2 desc")

It should not have any cars other than Buick. Unless I add the condition on data frame a, it enforces the condition only on b. This is not the way it works in SQL.

Thoughts?

Thanks.

1, There is no Auto2 in ISLR.

2. If by Auto2 you meant Auto then since the join is only on cylinders and not on cylinders and name the joined table will contain names other than buick.

messages.subject: Unused arguments error on .local() when loading from file.
messages.subject_clean: Unused arguments error on .local() when loading from file.
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am trying to open a big file (~3GB) using sqlfd. I've just installed sqldf 0.4.9 on R version 3.1.1 for Mac OS X 10.9.2.

While trying to open the file like this:

f <- file("preprocessed.csv")
df <-sqldf("select * from f")

I get the following error:

Error in .local(conn, name, value, ...) :
  unused arguments (comment.char = "", quote = "\"")

The same happens when I use read.csv.sql().

What am I doing wrong?

Thank you.

Best regards

On Thursday, October 30, 2014 5:10:11 PM UTC-4, Fabio Eitelvein wrote:
> Hi there,
>
> I am trying to open a big file (~3GB) using sqlfd. I've just installed sqldf 0.4.9 on R version 3.1.1 for Mac OS X 10.9.2.
>
> While trying to open the file like this:
>
> f <- file("preprocessed.csv")
> df <-sqldf("select * from f")
>
> I get the following error:
>
> Error in .local(conn, name, value, ...) :
>   unused arguments (comment.char = "", quote = "\"")
>
> The same happens when I use read.csv.sql().

Those arguments are not available.  sqldf and read.csv.sql uses sqlite to read in the data and sqlite is more limited than read.table in the range of arguments available.

See ?sqldf

In looking at this further there is an additional difference in RSQLite 1.0.0 (relative to the prior version) that was recently uploaded to CRAN that causes this.

A fix is in googlecode repo at http://sqldf.googlecode.com .

Until this fixed version is on CRAN you can:

   1. build the new version from source, or

   2. source the fixed sqldf.R on the fly like this:

   library(sqldf)
   source("http://sqldf.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/R/sqldf.R")
   ... your code ...
